newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan opposition closes Pakistan consulate.
newsitem.headline: Afghan opposition closes Pakistan consulate.

text.p: The authorities in the opposition-held northern Afghan city of Mazar-i-Sharif announced on Friday that they were closing Pakistan's consulate there.

The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) reported that opposition leader General Abdul Malik had said the people of Mazar-i-Sharif were angry at what he called Pakistan's support for the Islamic Taleban militia.
He said he had decided to shut the consulate temporarily as a security precaution in case it came under attack from local people.
Remaining consulate staff should leave for their own safety, he was quoted as saying.
Pakistani diplomats were evacuated from Mazar-i-Sharif at the end of May when Malik's troops, backed by the Shi'ite Moslem Hizb-i-Wahdat militia, drove the Taleban from the city.

Pakistan became the first country formally to recognise the Taleban government in Kabul on May 25, the day after the purist Islamic militia moved into Mazar-i-Sharif, thanks to an alliance with Malik which swiftly collapsed into bitter fighting.
No immediate comment from Pakistani officials was available.
Pakistan has denied backing the Taleban, who captured Kabul in September. Islamabad says it is trying to promote dialogue among Afghans to bring peace to the war-shattered country.
